components.note: 目 (eye) — sight, as in 看, 睛, 睡.
艮 (gèn) is a loose sound clue for yǎn; 艮 also sounds out 跟 gēn, 很 hěn and 根 gēn.
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.

example.hanzi: 在父母眼中,孩子永远是孩子。
example.pinyin: Zài fùmǔ yǎnzhōng, háizi yǒngyuǎn shì háizi.
example.english: In parents' eyes, children are always children.
example.fact: The human eye can distinguish around 10 million different colors, according to research on color perception, yet contains only three types of cone cells sensitive to red, green, and blue wavelengths of light — all perceived color arises from the brain combining signals from just these three receptor types.

examples.hanzi: 在孩子眼中,爸爸是最强的英雄。
examples.pinyin: Zài háizi yǎnzhōng, bàba shì zuì qiáng de yīngxióng.
examples.english: In a child's eyes, Dad is the strongest hero.

examples.hanzi: 他眼中充满了泪水。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǎnzhōng chōngmǎnle lèishuǐ.
examples.english: His eyes were filled with tears.

components.note: 目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; to meet is to cross paths.
禺 (yú) is close to yù; same part in 愚 yú and 偶 ǒu.

example.hanzi: 他们在一次旅行中意外相遇。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài yī cì lǚxíng zhōng yìwài xiāngyù.
example.english: They unexpectedly met each other during a trip.
example.fact: Voyager 1, launched by NASA in 1977, used a rare gravitational alignment of Jupiter and Saturn to slingshot itself toward interstellar space; it is now the most distant human-made object from Earth, and its trajectory depended on a planetary arrangement that occurs only about once every 176 years.

examples.hanzi: 我们在火车上意外相遇,聊了一路。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài huǒchē shàng yìwài xiāngyù, liáole yí lù.
examples.english: We unexpectedly met on the train and chatted the whole way.

examples.hanzi: 两条河在这里相遇,汇成了一条大河。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng tiáo hé zài zhèlǐ xiāngyù, huìchéngle yì tiáo dà hé.
examples.english: Two rivers meet here and merge into one big river.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money and value, as in 财, 买; 质 is the real value or substance of something.
里 (village, unit) — the bottom; the dictionary takes it as the 'unit/measure' part, as in 重量 weight, 能量. 里 is also a Chinese mile.
旦 (dàn, dawn) — the top. A loose sound clue only today: liáng/liàng vs dàn. Do not rely on it.

example.hanzi: 这台机器的质量非常好。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái jīqì de zhìliàng fēicháng hǎo.
example.english: This machine's quality is very good.
example.fact: The kilogram was redefined in 2019 by the International Bureau of Weights and Measures to be based on Planck's constant rather than a physical platinum-iridium cylinder kept in France since 1889 — the last of the seven SI base units to abandon a physical artifact in favor of a definition rooted in fundamental constants of nature.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅的服务质量很高。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de fúwù zhìliàng hěn gāo.
examples.english: This restaurant's service quality is high.

examples.hanzi: 买东西时,我更看重质量,不是价格。
examples.pinyin: Mǎi dōngxi shí, wǒ gèng kànzhòng zhìliàng, bú shì jiàgé.
examples.english: When shopping, I care more about quality than price.

components.note: 儿 (legs, person) — with a foot 𠂉 above: a foot stepping out in front of a person, so "first, earlier".
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.

example.hanzi: 这家公司使用了非常先进的技术。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī shǐyòng le fēicháng xiānjìn de jìshù.
example.english: This company uses very advanced technology.
example.fact: The James Webb Space Telescope, launched in December 2021, unfolded a sunshield the size of a tennis court and a 6.5-meter gold-coated beryllium mirror after reaching its observation point nearly 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, at a location called the second Lagrange point where gravitational forces let it hold a stable position relative to the Earth and Sun.

examples.hanzi: 这个国家的医疗设备非常先进。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de yīliáo shèbèi fēicháng xiānjìn.
examples.english: This country's medical equipment is very advanced.

examples.hanzi: 他被评为学校的先进工作者。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi píngwéi xuéxiào de xiānjìn gōngzuòzhě.
examples.english: He was named an outstanding worker at the school.

components.note: 心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.
子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.

example.hanzi: 她大学时主修心理学。
example.pinyin: Tā dàxué shí zhǔxiū xīnlǐxué.
example.english: She majored in psychology in college.
example.fact: Wilhelm Wundt opened the first laboratory dedicated exclusively to psychological research in Leipzig, Germany, in 1879, a milestone widely regarded as marking psychology's emergence as a distinct experimental science separate from philosophy.

examples.hanzi: 她很喜欢心理学,想以后当心理医生。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn xǐhuan xīnlǐxué, xiǎng yǐhòu dāng xīnlǐ yīshēng.
examples.english: She loves psychology and wants to become a therapist later.

examples.hanzi: 这本心理学的书很容易读懂。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn xīnlǐxué de shū hěn róngyì dúdǒng.
examples.english: This psychology book is easy to understand.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.
口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
彐 (broom top, from 帚) — in the old form 歸 a woman with a broom 帚 'returns' to her husband's home; the story is a traditional account, not proven.
追 (zhuī) — the old form 歸 is said to use 追-like parts for sound; guī is only a loose match. Treat as a memory aid, not a rule.

example.hanzi: 地震过后,许多人无家可归。
example.pinyin: Dìzhèn guòhòu, xǔduō rén wú jiā kě guī.
example.english: After the earthquake, many people were left homeless.
example.fact: The 1976 Tangshan earthquake in northern China, measuring around magnitude 7.8, struck a densely populated industrial city with little warning in the middle of the night and is estimated to have killed several hundred thousand people, making it one of the deadliest earthquakes of the 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 冬天有很多流浪猫无家可归。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān yǒu hěn duō liúlàng māo wújiākěguī.
examples.english: In winter, many stray cats have no home.

examples.hanzi: 他失业以后,一度无家可归。
examples.pinyin: Tā shīyè yǐhòu, yídù wújiākěguī.
examples.english: After losing his job, he was homeless for a while.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室.
玉 (jade) — jade kept under a roof: treasure. The traditional 寶 also had 贝 (cowrie, money).
贝 (shell, old money) — value and price, as in 财 wealth, 买 buy, 费 fee.

example.hanzi: 时间是最宝贵的财富。
example.pinyin: Shíjiān shì zuì bǎoguì de cáifù.
example.english: Time is the most valuable wealth.
example.fact: The most precise atomic clocks today, based on the vibrations of cesium or strontium atoms, are accurate to within one second over roughly 15 billion years — longer than the current age of the universe — and they underpin the GPS satellite network, where even nanosecond-level timing errors can translate into positioning errors of several meters.

examples.hanzi: 谢谢你给我提了这么宝贵的意见。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ gěi wǒ tíle zhème bǎoguì de yìjiàn.
examples.english: Thank you for giving me such valuable advice.

examples.hanzi: 我们要宝贵每一天,好好学习。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào bǎoguì měi yì tiān, hǎohāo xuéxí.
examples.english: We should treasure every day and study hard.

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — a bird over a flame is scorched. 焦 also sounds out 蕉 jiāo and 礁 jiāo.
灬 (fire, 四点底) — flames at the bottom, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 煮 cook.

example.hanzi: 面包烤焦了。
example.pinyin: Miànbāo kǎo jiāo le.
example.english: The bread got burnt.
example.fact: 焦 is burnt: 焦糖 (caramel), 烤焦. By extension it describes burning worry: 焦虑 (anxiety), 焦急 (anxious). 焦点 (focus) and 焦距 (focal length) come from the same idea of a focal point.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈焦急地等着我的电话。
examples.pinyin: Māma jiāojí de děng zhe wǒ de diànhuà.
examples.english: Mom waited anxiously for my call.

examples.hanzi: 锅里的菜已经煮焦了，不能吃了。
examples.pinyin: Guōlǐ de cài yǐjīng zhǔ jiāo le, bù néng chī le.
examples.english: The food in the pot has been cooked until burnt.

components.note: 自 (self/nose) — the middle part, as in 臭 smell; it does not explain 'summer'. Memory aid: your own nose feeling the heat.
夂 (go slowly) — the bottom part and radical, a foot. The old form shows a figure in ceremonial dress; as a memory aid only.

example.hanzi: 夏天太热了，我想去海边。
example.pinyin: Xiàtiān tài rè le, wǒ xiǎng qù hǎibiān.
example.english: Summer is too hot, I want to go to the seaside.
example.fact: 夏 is also an old name for China: 华夏 and the Xia dynasty, traditionally the first dynasty. Related: 夏令营 (summer camp) and 夏至 (the summer solstice, one of the 24 solar terms).

examples.hanzi: 夏天我们常常去游泳。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān wǒmen chángcháng qù yóuyǒng.
examples.english: In summer we often go swimming.

examples.hanzi: 今年的夏季特别长。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián de xiàjì tèbié cháng.
examples.english: This year's summer season is especially long.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and discussion: 说, 议, 谈; 论 is debate and theory.
仑 (lún) gives the sound; same part in 轮 lún and 伦 lún.

example.hanzi: 我们来讨论一下这个问题。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen lái tǎolùn yíxià zhège wèntí.
example.english: Let's discuss this question.
example.fact: 论 builds 讨论 (to discuss), 理论 (theory), 论文 (a thesis or paper), 结论 (conclusion) and 无论 (no matter what). 论斤卖 means selling by weight.

examples.hanzi: 他们在会议上讨论新的计划。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài huìyì shàng tǎolùn xīn de jìhuà.
examples.english: They discussed the new plan at the meeting.

examples.hanzi: 无论天气怎么样，我都会去跑步。
examples.pinyin: Wúlùn tiānqì zěnmeyàng, wǒ dōu huì qù pǎobù.
examples.english: No matter what the weather is like, I will go running.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — payment and loss, as in 财 wealth, 买 buy.
咅 (pōu) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 陪 péi and 培 péi.

example.hanzi: 你打坏了我的杯子，要赔我。
example.pinyin: Nǐ dǎhuài le wǒ de bēizi, yào péi wǒ.
example.english: You broke my cup, so you should pay me back.
example.fact: 赔 is about money: 赔钱 (to lose money), 赔偿 (to compensate), 赔礼道歉 (to apologize with a gift). It is a homophone of 陪 (péi, to accompany); the 贝 radical points to money.

examples.hanzi: 如果弄坏了，我会照价赔偿。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ nòng huài le, wǒ huì zhàojià péicháng.
examples.english: If I break it, I will compensate you at the full price.

examples.hanzi: 他做生意赔了不少钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuò shēngyi péi le bù shǎo qián.
examples.english: He lost quite a lot of money in his business.

components.note: 真 (zhēn) is a sound clue for 镇 zhèn and 慎 shèn; 真 means real, true.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 科学家们不断探索自然界的真理。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiāmen bùduàn tànsuǒ zìránjiè de zhēnlǐ.
example.english: Scientists continuously explore the truths of the natural world.
example.fact: Galileo Galilei's telescopic observations of Jupiter's four largest moons in 1610 provided some of the earliest direct evidence against the geocentric model of the universe, since the moons clearly orbited Jupiter rather than Earth — a finding that put him in direct conflict with church doctrine and eventually led to his trial by the Roman Inquisition in 1633.

examples.hanzi: 这个理论最终被证明是真理。
examples.pinyin: Zhège lǐlùn zuìzhōng bèi zhèngmíng shì zhēnlǐ.
examples.english: This theory was eventually proven to be the truth.

examples.hanzi: 真理往往掌握在少数人手里。
examples.pinyin: Zhēnlǐ wǎngwǎng zhǎngwò zài shǎoshù rén shǒu lǐ.
examples.english: The truth is often held by a few people.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth family: 布, 带, 帽. Memory aid: a market stall with a cloth banner 巾 under a roof 亠, i.e. a 市 market.
柿 (shì, persimmon) — contains 市 as a sound part, same sound shì.
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 我们的办公室在市中心。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen de bàngōngshì zài shìzhōngxīn.
example.english: Our office is downtown.
example.fact: Manhattan's street grid, laid out by the Commissioners' Plan of 1811, imposed a rigid pattern of numbered streets and avenues across most of the island well before the city grew to fill it, a rare example of urban planning that anticipated growth decades ahead of the population it would eventually serve.

examples.hanzi: 我周末喜欢去市中心逛街。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò xǐhuan qù shì zhōngxīn guàng jiē.
examples.english: I like going shopping downtown on weekends.

examples.hanzi: 市中心的房子又贵又小。
examples.pinyin: Shì zhōngxīn de fángzi yòu guì yòu xiǎo.
examples.english: Houses in the city center are expensive and small.

components.note: 来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.
亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.

example.hanzi: 我今天收到了一封来信。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān shōudào le yī fēng láixìn.
example.english: I received a letter today.
example.fact: The Pony Express, which operated for only about 18 months in 1860-1861, used relays of horseback riders to carry mail nearly 3,200 kilometers between Missouri and California in about 10 days — a dramatic improvement over previous overland routes that became obsolete almost overnight once the transcontinental telegraph was completed.

examples.hanzi: 读者来信说,他很喜欢这篇文章。
examples.pinyin: Dúzhě láixìn shuō, tā hěn xǐhuan zhè piān wénzhāng.
examples.english: A reader wrote in to say he really enjoyed this article.

examples.hanzi: 我已经回了你的来信,请查收。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng huíle nǐ de láixìn, qǐng cháshōu.
examples.english: I've replied to your letter, so please check it.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 给; 级 first meant the order of threads, then rank.
及 (jí) sounds exactly like 级; also 极 jí, 吸 xī.
刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 刻; to cut apart means separate.
另 (lìng, other) — separating things into "other" parts: 别 is another, different, or "don't".

example.hanzi: 这次考试分成不同的级别。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì fēnchéng bùtóng de jíbié.
example.english: This exam is divided into different levels.
example.fact: The Japanese martial art of judo introduced the now widespread colored-belt ranking system in the late 19th century under founder Jigoro Kano, originally using just white and black belts to mark beginner and advanced practitioners before later schools expanded it into the multi-color system familiar today.

examples.hanzi: 学生们按水平分成不同的级别。
examples.pinyin: Xuéshengmen àn shuǐpíng fēnchéng bùtóng de jíbié.
examples.english: The students are divided into different levels according to their ability.

examples.hanzi: 他的级别比我高,我得听他的。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jíbié bǐ wǒ gāo, wǒ děi tīng tā de.
examples.english: His rank is higher than mine, so I have to listen to him.

components.note: 马 (horse) — a galloping horse. As a radical it marks horses: 骑 ride, 驾 drive. It gives sound to 妈 mā, 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.
⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and travel: 跑, 跳, 跟; 路 is a road.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 洛 luò, 落 luò, 客 kè.

example.hanzi: 过马路的时候要看红绿灯。
example.pinyin: Guò mǎlù de shíhou yào kàn hónglǜdēng.
example.english: You should watch the traffic lights when crossing the street.
example.fact: The world's first electric traffic signal was installed in Cleveland, Ohio, in 1914, using red and green lights controlled manually from a booth; the now-familiar three-color signal with a separate yellow caution light wasn't patented until 1923, by inventor Garrett Morgan.

examples.hanzi: 这条马路晚上很安静。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo mǎlù wǎnshang hěn ānjìng.
examples.english: This street is very quiet at night.

examples.hanzi: 小朋友,别在马路上跑。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎopéngyou, bié zài mǎlù shàng pǎo.
examples.english: Kids, don't run on the road.

components.note: 立 (stand) — traditional 競 shows two people standing side by side in competition; 竞 keeps 立 and one 兄.
贝 (cowrie) — money and value, as in 财, 货, 买: competing for prizes was once tied to offerings and stakes.

example.hanzi: 他在数学竞赛中获得了第一名。
example.pinyin: Tā zài shùxué jìngsài zhōng huòdé le dì yī míng.
example.english: He won first place in the math competition.
example.fact: The International Mathematical Olympiad, first held in Romania in 1959 with just seven participating countries, has grown into the world's largest and most prestigious math competition for pre-university students, now drawing well over 100 countries each year and often serving as an early proving ground for future Fields Medal winners.

examples.hanzi: 学校下个月举办英语竞赛。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào xià gè yuè jǔbàn Yīngyǔ jìngsài.
examples.english: The school is holding an English contest next month.

examples.hanzi: 这两家公司在市场上竞赛得很激烈。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng jiā gōngsī zài shìchǎng shàng jìngsài de hěn jīliè.
examples.english: These two companies compete fiercely in the market.

components.note: 三 — three strokes, one more than 二. The numbers 一 二 三 are the only ones counted by drawing lines.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 会议将在下午三点开始。
example.pinyin: Huìyì jiāng zài xiàwǔ sān diǎn kāishǐ.
example.english: The meeting will start at three o'clock in the afternoon.
example.fact: Mechanical clocks with escapements — the mechanism that regulates a clock's ticking speed — first appeared in European monasteries around the late 13th century, built primarily to ensure monks woke for prayers at precise hours, well before clock faces with hour hands became common on public buildings.

examples.hanzi: 我每天早上三点就醒了,太早了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang sān diǎn jiù xǐng le, tài zǎo le.
examples.english: I wake up at three every morning, which is way too early.

examples.hanzi: 这个句子末尾要加三点,表示没说完。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jùzi mòwěi yào jiā sān diǎn, biǎoshì méi shuō wán.
examples.english: You add three dots at the end of this sentence to show it isn't finished.

components.note: 水 (water) — water and flow: 永 first meant a long river. 泳 yǒng (swimming) added the water radical later.

example.hanzi: 我永远不会忘记你。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yǒngyuǎn bú huì wàngjì nǐ.
example.english: I will never forget you.
example.fact: 永 gives 永远 (forever), 永久 (permanent), 永恒 (eternal), 永不 (never). In calligraphy, 永 is famous as the character that contains all eight basic brush strokes, practiced in the 永字八法.

examples.hanzi: 这家店永远都是满座的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn yǒngyuǎn dōu shì mǎnzuò de.
examples.english: This restaurant is always full.

examples.hanzi: 他们希望友谊永存。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen xīwàng yǒuyì yǒng cún.
examples.english: They hope their friendship will last forever.

meanings: it had not occurred to me

components.note: 心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 思, 感, 急: to think of someone.
相 (xiāng) is a close sound clue for xiǎng; 相 also in 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 真想不到你会来参加这次聚会。
example.pinyin: Zhēn xiǎngbudào nǐ huì lái cānjiā zhè cì jùhuì.
example.english: I really didn't expect you to come to this gathering.
example.fact: Penicillin was discovered by accident in 1928 when Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming noticed that a mold, Penicillium notatum, had contaminated one of his bacterial culture plates and was killing the surrounding bacteria — an observation from a messy lab that led directly to the development of the first widely used antibiotic.

examples.hanzi: 想不到这么小的城市也有地铁。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎng bú dào zhème xiǎo de chéngshì yě yǒu dìtiě.
examples.english: I never expected such a small city to have a subway.

examples.hanzi: 想不到他做饭这么好吃。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎng bú dào tā zuòfàn zhème hǎochī.
examples.english: Who would have thought he cooks so well?

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.
日 (sun) — marks light and time, as in 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; the sun over 京 gives a bright scene, hence scenery.
京 (jīng) gives the sound: 景 jǐng is close, as in 影 yǐng and 惊 jīng.

example.hanzi: 那个感人的情景让我至今难忘。
example.pinyin: Nàge gǎnrén de qíngjǐng ràng wǒ zhìjīn nánwàng.
example.english: That touching scene remains unforgettable to me even now.
example.fact: Psychologists use the term 'flashbulb memory' to describe the vivid, detailed recollections people often report for the moment they learned of a major shocking event — though research since the term was coined in 1977 has shown these memories, however vivid they feel, are not actually more accurate than ordinary memories and can shift substantially over time.

examples.hanzi: 在这样的情景下,他不知道该说什么。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhèyàng de qíngjǐng xià, tā bù zhīdào gāi shuō shénme.
examples.english: In such a situation, he didn't know what to say.

examples.hanzi: 老师让我们表演一个买东西的情景。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī ràng wǒmen biǎoyǎn yí gè mǎi dōngxi de qíngjǐng.
examples.english: The teacher asked us to act out a shopping scene.

components.note: 贝 (cowrie) — money and value, as in 财, 货, 买: competing for prizes was once tied to offerings and stakes.
禾 (grain) — crops and seasons, as in 种 plant, 秋 autumn, 稻 rice.
子 (child) — 季 was the youngest child, then the last month of a season, then the season itself.

example.hanzi: 这支球队在新赛季表现出色。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī qiúduì zài xīn sàijì biǎoxiàn chūsè.
example.english: This team has performed excellently in the new season.
example.fact: The NBA's regular season expanded from a shorter schedule when the league formed in 1946 to the modern 82-game format adopted in the 1967-68 season, a schedule length that has remained essentially unchanged for more than five decades despite ongoing debate about player fatigue and injury risk.

examples.hanzi: 新赛季下个月开始,球迷们很期待。
examples.pinyin: Xīn sàijì xià gè yuè kāishǐ, qiúmímen hěn qīdài.
examples.english: The new season starts next month, and fans are looking forward to it.

examples.hanzi: 他整个赛季都没有受过伤。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhěnggè sàijì dōu méiyǒu shòuguo shāng.
examples.english: He wasn't injured once the entire season.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: to look carefully inside.
祭 (jì) is a loose sound clue for chá; 祭 also sounds out 际 jì and 擦 cā.
见 (see) — seeing and perceiving, as in 现, 看, 视: 觉 is to sense and become aware (jué), also "sleep" (jiào) in 睡觉.
The top is a shape of 学 (xué), a loose sound hint from the traditional 覺.

example.hanzi: 她察觉到了空气中的一丝异味。
example.pinyin: Tā chájué dào le kōngqì zhōng de yī sī yìwèi.
example.english: She sensed a faint strange smell in the air.
example.fact: The human nose can distinguish more than one trillion different odors, according to a 2014 study published in Science, a figure far higher than the previously assumed range of about 10,000 — overturning decades of textbook estimates about the limits of human smell.

examples.hanzi: 我没有察觉他已经离开了房间。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu chájué tā yǐjīng líkāile fángjiān.
examples.english: I didn't notice that he had left the room.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈很快察觉到我心情不好。
examples.pinyin: Māma hěn kuài chájué dào wǒ xīnqíng bù hǎo.
examples.english: Mom quickly sensed that I was in a bad mood.

components.note: 疒 (illness, 病字旁) — sickness and pain: 疼 ache, 痛 pain, 瘦 thin; here the word for illness itself.
丙 (bǐng) is a near sound match for bìng; also in 柄 bǐng handle.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.

example.hanzi: 医生每天都会检查病人的病情。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng měitiān dōu huì jiǎnchá bìngrén de bìngqíng.
example.english: The doctor checks the patient's condition every day.
example.fact: Florence Nightingale, working as a nurse during the Crimean War in the 1850s, pioneered the systematic use of statistics in medicine, using data visualizations she called 'coxcomb' diagrams to show that far more soldiers were dying from preventable diseases in unsanitary hospitals than from battlefield wounds — work that helped drive major reforms in hospital hygiene.

examples.hanzi: 医生说爷爷的病情已经稳定了。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō yéye de bìngqíng yǐjīng wěndìng le.
examples.english: The doctor said Grandpa's condition has stabilized.

examples.hanzi: 他的病情突然变严重了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de bìngqíng tūrán biàn yánzhòng le.
examples.english: His condition suddenly became serious.

components.note: 女 (woman) — marks women, as in 妈, 姐, 好; 妆 is make-up.
丬 (a form of 爿) hints at the sound: 妆 zhuāng, close to 壮 zhuàng, 状 zhuàng and 装 zhuāng.

example.hanzi: 她每天早上化妆。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang huà zhuāng.
example.english: She puts on makeup every morning.
example.fact: 妆 builds 化妆 (to put on makeup), 化妆品 (cosmetics), 卸妆 (to remove makeup), 淡妆 / 浓妆 (light/heavy makeup) and 嫁妆 (a bride's trousseau).

examples.hanzi: 她每次出门前都要化妆。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi cì chūmén qián dōu yào huàzhuāng.
examples.english: She puts on makeup every time before going out.

examples.hanzi: 这个口红和你的妆很配。
examples.pinyin: Zhège kǒuhóng hé nǐ de zhuāng hěn pèi.
examples.english: This lipstick goes well with your makeup.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — hand actions; 搅 is to stir, as in 打 hit, 拉 pull.
觉 (jiào/jué) gives a close sound, as in 睡觉 shuì jiào.

example.hanzi: 请把咖啡搅一搅。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ kāfēi jiǎo yi jiǎo.
example.english: Please stir the coffee.
example.fact: 搅 means to stir: 搅拌 (to mix), 搅拌机 (a blender). It also means to disturb: 打搅 ("sorry to disturb you"), 搅乱 (to mess up), 搅局 (to spoil the occasion).

examples.hanzi: 他用勺子搅拌杯里的牛奶。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng sháozi jiǎobàn bēi lǐ de niúnǎi.
examples.english: He stirs the milk in the cup with a spoon.

examples.hanzi: 别来搅我，我在写作业。
examples.pinyin: Bié lái jiǎo wǒ, wǒ zài xiě zuòyè.
examples.english: Don't disturb me, I am doing my homework.

components.note: 医 (doctor) — simplified from 醫, which had 酉 (medicinal wine, as in 酒) at the bottom; the box 匚 and arrow 矢 remain.

example.hanzi: 她是一名医生。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yì míng yīshēng.
example.english: She is a doctor.
example.fact: 医 builds 医生 (doctor), 医院 (hospital), 医药 (medicine), 看医生 (to see a doctor). The traditional form 醫 also has 酉 (alcohol), since wine was used as medicine; the simplified form dropped it.

examples.hanzi: 我明天要去医院看医生。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān yào qù yīyuàn kàn yīshēng.
examples.english: Tomorrow I am going to the hospital to see a doctor.

examples.hanzi: 这位老中医的医术很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎo zhōngyī de yīshù hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This old doctor of Chinese medicine is very skilled.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 概 first meant a wooden scraper that levelled grain.
既 (jì) is a close sound clue for gài; 既 also in 溉 gài and 慨 kǎi.
心 (heart) — 心 marks thoughts and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感; 念 is to think of someone.
今 (jīn) — loose hint — 念 is niàn; 今 also sounds out 琴 qín and 含 hán, and means "now".

example.hanzi: 这是一个很难理解的抽象概念。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yī gè hěn nán lǐjiě de chōuxiàng gàiniàn.
example.english: This is an abstract concept that's very difficult to understand.
example.fact: The concept of zero as a number in its own right, rather than merely a placeholder, was formally developed in India, with the mathematician Brahmagupta providing rules for arithmetic with zero around 628 AD — a conceptual leap that took centuries longer to be adopted in Europe, where Roman numerals had no symbol for zero at all.

examples.hanzi: 老师用图片给我们解释这个新概念。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī yòng túpiàn gěi wǒmen jiěshì zhège xīn gàiniàn.
examples.english: The teacher explained this new concept to us with pictures.

examples.hanzi: 他对时间一点概念都没有,总是迟到。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì shíjiān yìdiǎn gàiniàn dōu méiyǒu, zǒngshì chídào.
examples.english: He has no sense of time at all and is always late.

components.note: 龶 (plant-like top) — dictionary reads the top as 'a poisonous plant'. Memory aid: a plant growing on top of a mother (母) is something you must not eat.
母 (mǔ, mother) — the bottom part and radical. Sound clue is lost today (毒 is dú); use it as a visual memory aid, as in 母亲.
艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 marks plants — medicine was made from herbs, as in 药 and 草.
约 (yuē) — near sound — 药 is yào; 约 also sounds out 钓 diào.

example.hanzi: 那部小说的凶手用毒药害死了受害者。
example.pinyin: Nà bù xiǎoshuō de xiōngshǒu yòng dúyào hàisǐ le shòuhàizhě.
example.english: The murderer in that novel killed the victim using poison.
example.fact: The 16th-century physician Paracelsus is credited with founding modern toxicology through his principle that 'the dose makes the poison' — meaning virtually any substance, even water or oxygen, can become toxic at a high enough dose, while many well-known poisons are harmless or even beneficial in small enough quantities.

examples.hanzi: 侦探发现杯子里有毒药。
examples.pinyin: Zhēntàn fāxiàn bēizi lǐ yǒu dúyào.
examples.english: The detective found poison in the cup.

examples.hanzi: 这种植物的汁可以做成毒药。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng zhíwù de zhī kěyǐ zuòchéng dúyào.
examples.english: The juice of this plant can be made into poison.

components.note: 子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.
月 (moon, month) — time and the moon: 明 bright, 朗 clear; in 期 it is a set period, as in 星期 week.
其 (qí) is the same sound with a different tone; also in 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī.

example.hanzi: 新学期从九月开始。
example.pinyin: Xīn xuéqī cóng jiǔyuè kāishǐ.
example.english: The new semester starts in September.
example.fact: The idea of a school calendar built around a long summer break traces back to 19th-century agrarian America, where children were needed to help harvest crops in the warm months. Many countries never adopted that pattern — Japan and South Korea, for instance, start their academic year in April, timed to the blooming of cherry blossoms rather than to any farm work.

examples.hanzi: 这个学期我选了五门课。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xuéqī wǒ xuǎnle wǔ mén kè.
examples.english: I'm taking five courses this semester.

examples.hanzi: 学期结束以后,我们就放寒假了。
examples.pinyin: Xuéqī jiéshù yǐhòu, wǒmen jiù fàng hánjià le.
examples.english: After the term ends, we'll have winter vacation.

components.note: 匸 (hiding box) — an enclosure for hiding, as in 区 district, 医 medicine.
若 (ruò) is only a loose sound clue.
口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.

example.hanzi: 他匿名捐赠了一百万美元。
example.pinyin: Tā nìmíng juānzèng le yìbǎiwàn měiyuán.
example.english: He anonymously donated one million dollars.
example.fact: Since the 1930s, a group of mostly French mathematicians has published foundational textbooks on rigorous mathematics under a single invented name, Nicolas Bourbaki, so that no individual author's reputation would attach to the work. The group still exists today, and 'Bourbaki' has never corresponded to a real person.

examples.hanzi: 这条评论是匿名发表的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo pínglùn shì nímíng fābiǎo de.
examples.english: This comment was posted anonymously.

examples.hanzi: 他想匿名给学校寄一封感谢信。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng nímíng gěi xuéxiào jì yì fēng gǎnxièxìn.
examples.english: He wants to send the school a thank-you letter anonymously.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 招 is to beckon with the hand.
召 (zhào) — near sound — 招 is zhāo; 召 also sounds out 照 zhào and 超 chāo.
彳 (step, left foot) — walking and roads: 行, 往, 很, 得; 待 is to go toward and wait on someone.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue; its family varies: 诗 shī, 持 chí, 特 tè, 等 děng.

example.hanzi: 主人热情地招待了客人。
example.pinyin: Zhǔrén rèqíng de zhāodài le kèrén.
example.english: The host warmly entertained the guests.
example.fact: In traditional Bedouin culture of the Arabian Peninsula, hospitality carries the weight of law: a guest, even a stranger or former rival, must be sheltered and fed for three days without being asked their business. The custom, known as diyafa, is thought to have arisen from the harsh conditions of desert travel, where turning a traveler away could mean their death.

examples.hanzi: 今晚我请你,我来招待你吃一顿好的。
examples.pinyin: Jīnwǎn wǒ qǐng nǐ, wǒ lái zhāodài nǐ chī yí dùn hǎo de.
examples.english: Tonight's on me; I'll treat you to a good meal.

examples.hanzi: 他们公司专门有人负责招待客户。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen gōngsī zhuānmén yǒu rén fùzé zhāodài kèhù.
examples.english: Their company has someone specifically in charge of hosting clients.

components.note: 言 (speech) — the traditional form of 讠: words and speech; an oath is a spoken promise.
折 (zhé, to break) — a promise you must not break; zhé is only a loose sound hint for shì.

example.hanzi: 他发誓永远爱她。
example.pinyin: Tā fāshì yǒngyuǎn ài tā.
example.english: He swore to love her forever.
example.fact: 誓 is a solemn vow: 发誓 (to swear), 誓言 (a pledge), 宣誓 (to take an oath), 誓不罢休 (to vow not to stop). 我发誓 ("I swear") is also used lightly in conversation.

examples.hanzi: 他们在婚礼上宣誓。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài hūnlǐ shàng xuānshì.
examples.english: They took their vows at the wedding.

examples.hanzi: 我对天发誓，我没有说谎。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì tiān fāshì, wǒ méiyǒu shuōhuǎng.
examples.english: I swear to heaven that I am not lying.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks soil and ground, as in 地 ground, 城 city wall, 坏 broken; 垫 is a cushion or pad put underneath.
执 (zhí) — loose sound hint (diàn vs zhí).

example.hanzi: 椅子上有一个软垫。
example.pinyin: Yǐzi shàng yǒu yí ge ruǎndiàn.
example.english: There is a soft cushion on the chair.
example.fact: 垫 means a pad: 垫子, 鼠标垫 (mouse pad). As a verb it means to pad or prop up, and in daily speech 垫钱 / 垫付 means to pay in advance for someone and be reimbursed later. 垫底 means to finish last.

examples.hanzi: 我在椅子上放了一个垫子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài yǐzi shàng fàng le yí ge diànzi.
examples.english: I put a cushion on the chair.

examples.hanzi: 你先帮我垫一下钱，回头还你。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān bāng wǒ diàn yíxià qián, huítóu huán nǐ.
examples.english: Please cover the money for me first and I will pay you back later.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech and talk: 说, 论, 请; 评 is to comment and judge.
平 (píng) sounds exactly like 评; also in 苹 píng.
刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) as in 到, 别, 利; 判 is to cut in half, so to separate and decide.
半 (bàn) — near sound — 判 is pàn; 半 means half.

example.hanzi: 裁判评判了这场比赛的结果。
example.pinyin: Cáipàn píngpàn le zhè chǎng bǐsài de jiéguǒ.
example.english: The referee judged the outcome of the match.
example.fact: After a vote-trading scandal at the 2002 Salt Lake City Olympics, the International Skating Union overhauled how figure skating is judged, replacing the old 6.0 scale with a detailed point system and, for a time, anonymous panels. The reform was meant to make scoring harder to manipulate, though critics still debate how much subjectivity it removed.

examples.hanzi: 评委们要评判每个选手的表现。
examples.pinyin: Píngwěimen yào píngpàn měi gè xuǎnshǒu de biǎoxiàn.
examples.english: The judges have to assess each contestant's performance.

examples.hanzi: 这种事不能随便评判,要先了解情况。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng shì bù néng suíbiàn píngpàn, yào xiān liǎojiě qíngkuàng.
examples.english: You can't judge such matters casually; understand the situation first.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; recognising something is naming it.
人 (rén) gives the exact sound, and also means "person".
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.

example.hanzi: 我认得这条街,以前来过。
example.pinyin: Wǒ rènde zhè tiáo jiē, yǐqián láiguo.
example.english: I recognize this street — I've been here before.
example.fact: In 1971, neuroscientist John O'Keefe discovered 'place cells' in the rat hippocampus that fire only when the animal is in a specific location, effectively forming an internal map that lets it recognize where it has been. The discovery, later extended to a full model of spatial navigation, earned O'Keefe a share of the 2014 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

examples.hanzi: 你认得这个字怎么念吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènde zhège zì zěnme niàn ma?
examples.english: Do you know how to pronounce this character?

examples.hanzi: 我不认得他,从来没见过。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú rènde tā, cónglái méi jiànguo.
examples.english: I don't know him; I've never met him.

components.note: 矢 (arrow) — the arrow was an ancient measure; also in 知 know, 矮 short, 射 shoot.
豆 (dòu) is only a loose sound clue for duǎn.
日 (sun) — 日 stands for day and time, as in 时, 晚, 早; 暂 is "for a short time".
斩 (zhǎn) — near sound — 暂 is zàn; 斩 also sounds out 渐 jiàn and 惭 cán.

example.hanzi: 这次相遇十分短暂。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì xiāngyù shífēn duǎnzàn.
example.english: This encounter was very brief.
example.fact: Mayflies spend one to three years as aquatic nymphs but live as winged adults for only a few hours to a couple of days, just long enough to mate and lay eggs before dying. Their scientific order name, Ephemeroptera, literally reflects that fleeting adult stage.

examples.hanzi: 夏天太短暂了,转眼就过去了。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān tài duǎnzàn le, zhuǎnyǎn jiù guòqù le.
examples.english: Summer is too short and passes in the blink of an eye.

examples.hanzi: 他的一生虽然短暂,却很精彩。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yìshēng suīrán duǎnzàn, què hěn jīngcǎi.
examples.english: His life was short, but it was wonderful.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the vertical stroke 丨 is the string being drawn back on a bow — 引 is to pull, then to attract and to cite.
寸 (hand, inch) — traditional 導 had 道 (road) plus 寸 (hand): a hand leading along a road; 道 dào is also a near-sound clue for 导 dǎo.

example.hanzi: 导游引导我们参观了故宫。
example.pinyin: Dǎoyóu yǐndǎo wǒmen cānguān le Gùgōng.
example.english: The tour guide led us through the Forbidden City.
example.fact: The Eddystone Lighthouse off the English coast was destroyed by storms and fire three times before engineer John Smeaton rebuilt it in 1759 using interlocking granite blocks shaped like a tree trunk. That design became the standard for lighthouse construction worldwide for the next two centuries.

examples.hanzi: 老师引导学生自己找出答案。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī yǐndǎo xuésheng zìjǐ zhǎochū dá'àn.
examples.english: The teacher guides the students to find the answer themselves.

examples.hanzi: 服务员引导我们走到了座位上。
examples.pinyin: Fúwùyuán yǐndǎo wǒmen zǒudàole zuòwèi shàng.
examples.english: The waiter led us to our seats.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.
衣 (clothing) — clothes and wear: 衬, 被, 袋; 装 is dress, then to pretend or to load.
壮 (zhuàng) is a near sound match for zhuāng; also in 状 zhuàng and 妆 zhuāng.

example.hanzi: 工人正在安装新的空调。
example.pinyin: Gōngrén zhèngzài ānzhuāng xīn de kōngtiáo.
example.english: Workers are installing the new air conditioner.
example.fact: Willis Carrier built the first modern air conditioner in 1902, not for human comfort but to control humidity at a Brooklyn printing plant where damp air was blurring the ink. Home air conditioning didn't become common in the United States until the 1950s.

examples.hanzi: 我的电脑需要安装新的软件。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de diànnǎo xūyào ānzhuāng xīn de ruǎnjiàn.
examples.english: My computer needs new software installed.

examples.hanzi: 师傅明天上午来安装热水器。
examples.pinyin: Shīfu míngtiān shàngwǔ lái ānzhuāng rèshuǐqì.
examples.english: The technician will come to install the water heater tomorrow morning.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — the lotus plant; also in 花 flower, 草 grass.
何 (hé) gives the exact sound.
兰 (orchid) — simplified from 蘭, which had the grass radical 艹 on top and 闌 giving the sound lán — a plant name.

example.hanzi: 荷兰以风车和郁金香闻名。
example.pinyin: Hélán yǐ fēngchē hé yùjīnxiāng wénmíng.
example.english: The Netherlands is famous for its windmills and tulips.
example.fact: During the Dutch 'tulip mania' of the 1630s, speculative prices for rare bulbs rose so high that by February 1637 a single bulb reportedly sold for more than ten times the annual income of a skilled craftsman. Economists still cite it as one of the earliest recorded speculative bubbles.

examples.hanzi: 我去年夏天去了荷兰旅游。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qùnián xiàtiān qùle Hélán lǚyóu.
examples.english: I traveled to the Netherlands last summer.

examples.hanzi: 荷兰的自行车比汽车还多。
examples.pinyin: Hélán de zìxíngchē bǐ qìchē hái duō.
examples.english: There are more bicycles than cars in the Netherlands.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads, as in 道 road, 追 chase.
豕 (pig) — the oldest form shows a foot chasing a pig, hence to pursue.
氵 (water) — slow seepage, little by little; also in 河 river, 海 sea.
斩 (zhǎn) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 暂 zàn and 惭 cán.

example.hanzi: 天色逐渐变暗了。
example.pinyin: Tiānsè zhújiàn biàn àn le.
example.english: The sky gradually grew dark.
example.fact: When Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912, he suggested landmasses creep apart at roughly the rate fingernails grow, a few centimeters a year. Decades later, plate tectonics confirmed the mechanism and showed the drift is powered by convection currents deep in the Earth's mantle.

examples.hanzi: 冬天来了,天气逐渐变冷。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān lái le, tiānqì zhújiàn biàn lěng.
examples.english: Winter has come and the weather is gradually getting colder.

examples.hanzi: 他的汉语水平在逐渐提高。
examples.pinyin: Tā de Hànyǔ shuǐpíng zài zhújiàn tígāo.
examples.english: His Chinese level is gradually improving.

components.note: 彡 (decorative strokes) — marks patterns and adornment, as in 形 shape, 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 修 is to tidy and decorate, then repair.
攸 (yōu) is only a loose hint for xiū; 悠 yōu shares it.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand holding a stick, as in 教 teach, 收 collect, 放 release: correcting by hand.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for gǎi.

example.hanzi: 他修改了论文的结论部分。
example.pinyin: Tā xiūgǎi le lùnwén de jiélùn bùfen.
example.english: He revised the conclusion section of his paper.
example.fact: Linus Torvalds wrote the Git version-control system in about two weeks in 2005, after a licensing dispute cut off the Linux kernel project's access to the commercial tool it had been using to track code revisions. Git went on to become the most widely used system for managing changes to software worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 请帮我修改一下这份简历。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ xiūgǎi yíxià zhè fèn jiǎnlì.
examples.english: Please help me revise this résumé.

examples.hanzi: 你可以修改自己的密码和头像。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ xiūgǎi zìjǐ de mìmǎ hé tóuxiàng.
examples.english: You can change your own password and profile picture.

meanings: to withdraw the mandate of heaven
(separable verb sometimes used in the pattern 革noun的命)

components.note: 革 — a hide stretched and scraped; also in 鞋 shoe, 鞭 whip. To renew, hence 革命 revolution.
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: an order is spoken.
令 (lìng, order) is a close sound clue for mìng; 令 also in 领 lǐng, 冷 lěng and 零 líng.

example.hanzi: 工业革命改变了整个世界。
example.pinyin: Gōngyè gémìng gǎibiàn le zhěnggè shìjiè.
example.english: The Industrial Revolution changed the entire world.
example.fact: The Industrial Revolution is usually dated from the 1760s, when James Watt's improvements made the steam engine efficient enough to power factories rather than just pump water out of mines. Within roughly a century, mechanized production had multiplied per-capita economic output in Britain far beyond anything seen in earlier human history.

examples.hanzi: 那场革命发生在一百多年前。
examples.pinyin: Nà chǎng gémìng fāshēng zài yì bǎi duō nián qián.
examples.english: That revolution took place over a hundred years ago.

examples.hanzi: 手机的出现带来了生活方式的革命。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī de chūxiàn dàiláile shēnghuó fāngshì de gémìng.
examples.english: The arrival of the mobile phone brought a revolution in lifestyle.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 进: to go and pick.
先 (xiān) is a close sound clue for xuǎn; 先 also in 洗 xǐ.
票 (ticket) — originally flames flying up, which is why 票 gives the sound piào/piāo to 漂 and 飘 and biāo to 标; ticket is a later meaning.

example.hanzi: 每个人只能投一张选票。
example.pinyin: Měi gèrén zhǐ néng tóu yì zhāng xuǎnpiào.
example.english: Each person can only cast one ballot.
example.fact: The secret ballot is sometimes called the 'Australian ballot' because South Australia was among the first places to adopt it, in 1856, letting voters mark their choices in private rather than announce them aloud. The United States did not widely adopt the practice until the 1890s, largely to curb vote-buying and intimidation at the polls.

examples.hanzi: 投票结束后,工作人员开始统计选票。
examples.pinyin: Tóupiào jiéshù hòu, gōngzuò rényuán kāishǐ tǒngjì xuǎnpiào.
examples.english: After voting ended, staff began counting the ballots.

examples.hanzi: 这张选票上的名字写错了,无效。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng xuǎnpiào shàng de míngzi xiěcuò le, wúxiào.
examples.english: The name on this ballot was written wrong, so it's invalid.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — mountain radical, as in 峰 peak, 岛 island, 岸 shore.
石 (rock) — stone on the mountain makes the cliff.
石 (stone) — a rock 口 at the foot of a cliff 厂; as a radical it marks stones and minerals, as in 破, 码, 砖, 磨.

example.hanzi: 这块岩石有几百万年的历史。
example.pinyin: Zhè kuài yánshí yǒu jǐ bǎiwàn nián de lìshǐ.
example.english: This rock is millions of years old.
example.fact: The Acasta Gneiss, exposed along a riverbank in Canada's Northwest Territories, has been dated to about 4.02 billion years old, making it one of the oldest known intact rock formations on Earth's surface. It formed less than 600 million years after the planet itself.

examples.hanzi: 山上的岩石又大又硬。
examples.pinyin: Shān shàng de yánshí yòu dà yòu yìng.
examples.english: The rocks on the mountain are big and hard.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们喜欢在海边的岩石上爬来爬去。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen xǐhuan zài hǎibiān de yánshí shàng pá lái pá qù.
examples.english: The children love climbing around on the rocks by the sea.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 女 marks women and feelings in old forms, as in 妒, 嫉; 嫌 is to dislike.
兼 (jiān) — near sound — 嫌 is xián; 兼 also sounds out 谦 qiān and 歉 qiàn.
疋 (foot) — the lower right. Dictionary story: an old man walking 疋 with a cane. Early forms show a person looking around, unsure. Treat as a memory aid.
矢 (arrow) — Dictionary reads it as a cane held by an old man; memory aid: an old man leaning on a stick, unsure which way — doubt, 怀疑.

example.hanzi: 警方怀疑他有嫌疑。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng huáiyí tā yǒu xiányí.
example.english: Police suspect that he is a suspect.
example.fact: The modern polygraph, invented by police officer John Larson in 1921, measures changes in heart rate, breathing, and skin conductivity rather than lies directly. Its scientific validity remains disputed, and polygraph results are inadmissible as evidence in most courts in the United States today.

examples.hanzi: 他有偷东西的嫌疑,警察正在调查。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu tōu dōngxi de xiányí, jǐngchá zhèngzài diàochá.
examples.english: He is suspected of stealing, and the police are investigating.

examples.hanzi: 证据不足,他的嫌疑已经被排除了。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngjù bùzú, tā de xiányí yǐjīng bèi páichú le.
examples.english: The evidence was insufficient, and suspicion against him has been cleared.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 迷 is losing one's way.
米 (mǐ) — near sound — 迷 is mí, the same syllable with a different tone.
心 (heart) — marks the mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 意; 惑 is a doubtful, confused heart.
或 (huò) gives the sound exactly: 惑 huò.

example.hanzi: 这道题把我迷惑了。
example.pinyin: Zhè dào tí bǎ wǒ míhuo le.
example.english: This problem confused me.
example.fact: The Ames room, designed by ophthalmologist Adelbert Ames Jr. in 1946, uses a distorted, trapezoidal shape and forced perspective to trick viewers into seeing people appear to shrink or grow dramatically as they walk across it. The illusion works only when viewed through a single peephole that hides the room's true geometry.

examples.hanzi: 你别说话了,你说得我越来越迷惑。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié shuōhuà le, nǐ shuō de wǒ yuè lái yuè míhuò.
examples.english: Stop talking; you're making me more and more confused.

examples.hanzi: 别被广告迷惑,买东西要多比较。
examples.pinyin: Bié bèi guǎnggào míhuò, mǎi dōngxi yào duō bǐjiào.
examples.english: Don't be misled by ads; compare more when you shop.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — 舟 is the boat radical, as in 般, 航, 舰; 船 is a ship.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 船员们正在检查设备。
example.pinyin: Chuányuánmen zhèngzài jiǎnchá shèbèi.
example.english: The crew members are checking the equipment.
example.fact: The RMS Titanic carried roughly 885 crew members in 1912, more than half of whom died when the ship sank. The disaster directly led to the first International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) in 1914, which set standards, still in use today, for lifeboat capacity and onboard safety equipment.

examples.hanzi: 这艘船上有二十名船员。
examples.pinyin: Zhè sōu chuán shàng yǒu èrshí míng chuányuán.
examples.english: There are twenty crew members on this ship.

examples.hanzi: 船员们在甲板上看日落。
examples.pinyin: Chuányuánmen zài jiǎbǎn shàng kàn rìluò.
examples.english: The crew watched the sunset on the deck.

components.note: 子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住.
立 (stand) — the spot where a person 亻 stands 立: a position or seat; also 位置 position.

example.hanzi: 她获得了博士学位。
example.pinyin: Tā huòdé le bóshì xuéwèi.
example.english: She earned a doctoral degree.
example.fact: The University of Bologna, founded in 1088, is generally regarded as the oldest continuously operating university in the world. Its early scholars helped establish the practice of formally examining students and granting degrees as recognized academic credentials.

examples.hanzi: 我在英国拿到了硕士学位。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài Yīngguó nádàole shuòshì xuéwèi.
examples.english: I earned my master's degree in the UK.

examples.hanzi: 他一边工作,一边读学位。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìbiān gōngzuò, yìbiān dú xuéwèi.
examples.english: He works while studying for a degree.

components.note: 干 (dry; do) — a forked pole or shield. It lends its sound to 肝 gān, 杆 gān, 赶 gǎn, 汗 hàn and 岸 àn.
氵 (water) — a stream to cross; also in 河 river, 游 swim.
步 (step) — steps through water: wading, hence being involved in something.

example.hanzi: 请不要干涉我的私事。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bùyào gānshè wǒ de sīshì.
example.english: Please don't interfere with my private affairs.
example.fact: In 1801, Thomas Young shone light through two narrow slits and observed a striped pattern on a screen behind them, evidence that light waves were interfering with each other much like ripples on water. The double-slit experiment remains one of the clearest demonstrations that light behaves as a wave.

examples.hanzi: 父母不应该干涉孩子的交友。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ bù yīnggāi gānshè háizi de jiāoyǒu.
examples.english: Parents shouldn't interfere in their children's friendships.

examples.hanzi: 别人的家事,我们不方便干涉。
examples.pinyin: Biéren de jiāshì, wǒmen bù fāngbiàn gānshè.
examples.english: It's inconvenient for us to interfere in other people's family matters.
